records.source: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν θεοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἡμῶν Τιμοθέῳ γνησίῳ τέκνῳ ἐν πίστει· χάρις, ἔλεος, εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus according to [the] command of God Savior of us and of Christ Jesus the hope of us, \v 2 to Timothy, genuine child in faith: grace, mercy, peace from God Father and Christ Jesus the Lord of us.
pieces: From Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus by the command of God our Savior and of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our hope,
to Timothy, my true son in the faith. Grace, mercy and peace to you from God the Father and from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

L.1: Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus by command of God our Savior and of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus our hope,
L.2: to Timothy, [my] true child in [the] faith: grace, mercy, peace from God [the] Father and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

R.1: This letter is from Paul. I am an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, because God our Savior and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, in whom we hope, gave me this work.
R.2: I am writing to Timothy. You are like a true son to me in the faith. I pray that God the Father and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord will show you grace and mercy and give you peace.

decisions.choice: the letter as Paul's, to Timothy in Ephesus
decisions.reason: The letter presents itself as written by Paul to his co-worker Timothy (Acts 16:1-3; Philippians 2:19-22), left in Ephesus to correct false teachers (verse 3). Since the nineteenth century many readers have questioned whether Paul wrote the letters to Timothy and Titus himself; the notes here describe what the letter says.

decisions.choice: by command of God our Savior
decisions.reason: ἐπιταγὴν is a royal command: Paul's apostleship rests on God's order. Calling God σωτῆρος ("Savior") is frequent in these letters (2:3; 4:10; Titus 1:3), as in the Old Testament (Psalm 24:5 in Greek; Isaiah 45:21).

decisions.choice: Christ Jesus our hope: the one their hope rests on
decisions.reason: Christ is himself the hope of believers (Colossians 1:27).

decisions.choice: a true child in the faith: Paul's son in faith
decisions.reason: γνησίῳ means genuine, legitimate. Timothy is Paul's child not by birth but by faith (1 Corinthians 4:17). The noun is neuter and the image is of a son.

decisions.choice: grace, mercy, peace
decisions.reason: Paul's usual greeting has "grace and peace"; the letters to Timothy add ἔλεος ("mercy"), as Jewish greetings did.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: son
decisions.reason: The image is of a father and his son (m4).

decisions.choice: because God our Savior and Christ Jesus, in whom we hope, gave me this work
alternatives: by command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope
decisions.reason: Readable says what "by command" means (m2, m3).

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: Καθὼς παρεκάλεσά σε προσμεῖναι ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, πορευόμενος εἰς Μακεδονίαν, ἵνα παραγγείλῃς τισὶν μὴ ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖν μηδὲ προσέχειν μύθοις καὶ γενεαλογίαις ἀπεράντοις, αἵτινες ἐκζητήσεις παρέχουσι μᾶλλον ἢ οἰκονομίαν θεοῦ τὴν ἐν πίστει τὸ δὲ τέλος τῆς παραγγελίας ἐστὶν ἀγάπη ἐκ καθαρᾶς καρδίας καὶ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς καὶ πίστεως ἀνυποκρίτου, ὧν τινες ἀστοχήσαντες ἐξετράπησαν εἰς ματαιολογίαν, θέλοντες εἶναι νομοδιδάσκαλοι, μὴ νοοῦντες μήτε ἃ λέγουσιν μήτε περὶ τίνων διαβεβαιοῦνται.
records.gloss: Just as I urged you to remain in Ephesus, going into Macedonia, so that you might command certain [ones] not to teach other doctrine \v 4 nor to pay attention to myths and genealogies endless, which speculations bring rather than [the] stewardship of God the [one] in faith, \v 5 the but goal of the command is love out of a pure heart and a conscience good and faith sincere, \v 6 from which some having missed the mark have turned aside to empty talk, \v 7 wanting to be teachers of the law, not understanding either what they say or concerning what things they confidently assert.
pieces: When I was leaving for Macedonia, I urged you to stay on in Ephesus, so that you could order certain people to stop teaching a different doctrine
and to stop giving their minds to myths and endless lists of ancestors. These lead to speculation rather than to God's plan, which works through faith.
The aim of our instruction is love that comes from a pure heart, a good conscience and a faith without pretense.
Some have missed this aim and wandered off into empty talk.
They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying, or the things they are so sure about.

L.3: As I urged you when I was going into Macedonia, to remain in Ephesus so that you might command certain [people] not to teach a different doctrine
L.4: or to devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculations rather than God's stewardship, which is by faith,
L.5: [so I urge you now]. But the goal of our command is love from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith.
L.6: Some, having missed the mark, have turned aside from these to empty talk,
L.7: wanting to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they are saying nor the things about which they make confident assertions.

R.3: When I left to go to Macedonia, I asked you to stay in the city of Ephesus. Some people there are teaching things that are not true, and I wanted you to tell them to stop.
R.4: Tell them to stop paying attention to made-up stories and long lists of ancestors that never end. These things only make people argue. They do not help them do God's work, which we do by faith.
R.5: The reason we tell you this is so that people will love each other. That love comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience and real faith.
R.6: Some people have turned away from these things. Now they only talk about things that do not matter.
R.7: They want to be teachers of God's law, but they do not understand what they are talking about, even when they speak with great confidence.

decisions.choice: the sentence is never finished
decisions.reason: Καθὼς ("just as") begins a comparison that never gets its main clause; "so I urge you now" is understood. Paul's thought runs straight on to the false teachers.

decisions.choice: Ephesus and Macedonia
decisions.reason: Ephesus, the chief city of the province of Asia, was where Paul had worked for over two years (Acts 19:1-20:1). Acts does not record the journey to Macedonia mentioned here.

decisions.choice: teach a different doctrine
decisions.reason: ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖν is a compound found first here: to teach something other than the apostles' teaching (6:3).

decisions.choice: myths and endless genealogies
decisions.reason: μύθοις is the word for stories and legends. The genealogies may be speculative expansions of the family lists in Genesis; the letter calls them "endless" and does not explain them further (Titus 1:14; 3:9).

decisions.choice: God's stewardship, which is by faith: God's ordering of salvation, received by faith
alternatives: God's training, edification (a different word in some manuscripts)
decisions.reason: οἰκονομίαν is the management of a household, and so God's plan or ordering of things (Ephesians 1:10). Some manuscripts have a similar word meaning "building up".

decisions.choice: the goal of the command: love from a pure heart, a good conscience and sincere faith
decisions.reason: τέλος is the aim or end. "The command" is the instruction Timothy is to give (verse 3). True teaching aims at love, while the false teaching produces argument.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law: teachers of the Jewish law
decisions.reason: νομοδιδάσκαλοι suggests that the teachers drew on the law of Moses, as verses 8-11 assume.

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable finish the opening sentence
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence is left unfinished (m1); Balanced and Readable make it a complete sentence.

decisions.choice: [so I urge you now]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the missing main clause (m1).

decisions.choice: lists of ancestors
decisions.reason: Plain words for "genealogies" (m4).

records.heading: Warning against a different doctrine

records.source: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι καλὸς ὁ νόμος ἐάν τις αὐτῷ νομίμως χρῆται, εἰδὼς τοῦτο, ὅτι δικαίῳ νόμος οὐ κεῖται, ἀνόμοις δὲ καὶ ἀνυποτάκτοις, ἀσεβέσι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς, ἀνοσίοις καὶ βεβήλοις, πατρολῴαις καὶ μητρολῴαις, ἀνδροφόνοις, πόρνοις, ἀρσενοκοίταις, ἀνδραποδισταῖς, ψεύσταις, ἐπιόρκοις, καὶ εἴ τι ἕτερον τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδασκαλίᾳ ἀντίκειται, κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς δόξης τοῦ μακαρίου θεοῦ, ὃ ἐπιστεύθην ἐγώ.
records.gloss: We know now that good [is] the law if anyone it lawfully uses, \v 9 knowing this, that for a righteous [person] law not is laid down, but for lawless and rebellious, ungodly and sinners, unholy and profane, killers of fathers and killers of mothers, murderers, \v 10 sexually immoral, men who lie with males, slave dealers, liars, perjurers, and if anything other to the healthy teaching is opposed, \v 11 according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was entrusted [to] me.
pieces: We know that the law is good, if it is used as it should be.

We know that law is not made for people who do right, but for the lawless and the rebellious, the ungodly and sinners, those who have no regard for what is holy, those who kill their fathers or mothers, murderers,
the sexually immoral, men who have sex with men, slave traders, liars, those who break their oaths, and whatever else goes against the sound teaching
that agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which has been entrusted to me.

L.8: Now we know that the law is good if one uses it lawfully,
L.9: knowing this, that law is not laid down for a righteous [person] but for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers and mothers, for murderers,
L.10: for the sexually immoral, men who lie with males, slave traders, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is opposed to sound teaching,
L.11: in keeping with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.

R.8: We know that God's law is good, when people use it in the right way.
R.9: We know that the law is not for people who do what is right. It is for people who do not obey any law and who will not be ruled. It is for people who do not respect God and who sin, for people who are not holy and who make fun of holy things. It is for people who kill their fathers or mothers, and for all who murder.
R.10: It is for people who commit sexual sins, for men who have sex with men, for people who kidnap others to sell as slaves, and for people who lie or break their promises. It is for anything else that goes against true teaching.
R.11: That teaching agrees with the good news about the glory of the blessed God. God gave me the work of telling this good news.

decisions.choice: uses it lawfully: uses the law for its proper purpose
decisions.reason: νομίμως ("lawfully") is a play on νόμος ("law"): the law is good when it is used as the law is meant to be used, to restrain and expose wrongdoing, not for speculation (verses 4, 7).

decisions.choice: the list follows the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: The list moves from sins against God (lawless, ungodly, unholy) to those against parents (Exodus 20:12), murder (20:13), sexual sin (20:14), kidnapping (20:15; Exodus 21:16) and false witness (20:16).

decisions.choice: men who have sexual relations with males
alternatives: particular exploitative forms, such as the abuse of boys
decisions.reason: ἀρσενοκοίταις is a rare word, first found in Paul (1 Corinthians 6:9). It joins "male" and "bed", the words the Greek Old Testament uses in Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13 for a man lying with a male. It stands here beside sexual immorality in the commandment against adultery. Readers disagree about its exact scope: some take it to cover all sexual relations between men, others particular practices of the time.

decisions.choice: slave traders: those who kidnap people to sell them
decisions.reason: ἀνδραποδισταῖς is a kidnapper or slave dealer, the sin the law punished with death (Exodus 21:16).

decisions.choice: sound teaching: healthy, life-giving teaching
decisions.reason: ὑγιαινούσῃ is "healthy", a favorite word of these letters (6:3; 2 Timothy 1:13; Titus 1:9): teaching that makes people spiritually well, unlike the teaching that "spreads like gangrene" (2 Timothy 2:17).

decisions.choice: the gospel of the glory of the blessed God: the gospel that reveals God's glory
decisions.reason: τῆς δόξης ("of the glory") may describe the gospel as glorious, or say that it tells of God's glory (2 Corinthians 4:4).

decisions.choice: entrusted with: given in trust
decisions.reason: πιστεύω usually means "believe", but in the passive with an object it means to be entrusted with something (Galatians 2:7; 1 Thessalonians 2:4).

decisions.choice: men who lie with males (L); men who have sex with men (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the parts of the word (m3); Balanced and Readable say the same in plain words. Words for orientation such as "homosexuals" say more than the Greek does.

decisions.choice: entrusted (L, B); God gave me the work (R)
decisions.reason: The sense here is "entrusted" (m7), so the key term "believe" is not used.

decisions.choice: glorious gospel
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the key term "glory" in "glorious" (m6).

records.heading: What the law is for

records.source: Χάριν ἔχω τῷ ἐνδυναμώσαντί με Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πιστόν με ἡγήσατο θέμενος εἰς διακονίαν, τὸ πρότερον ὄντα βλάσφημον καὶ διώκτην καὶ ὑβριστήν· ἀλλὰ ἠλεήθην, ὅτι ἀγνοῶν ἐποίησα ἐν ἀπιστίᾳ, ὑπερεπλεόνασεν δὲ ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν μετὰ πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: Thanks I have to the [one] having strengthened me, Christ Jesus the Lord of us, because faithful me he considered, appointing [me] to service, \v 13 the formerly being a blasphemer and a persecutor and a violent man; but I was shown mercy, because being ignorant I acted in unbelief, \v 14 overflowed but the grace of the Lord of us with faith and love the [ones] in Christ Jesus.
pieces: I thank {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord, who has given me strength, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judged me trustworthy and appointed me to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},

even though I used to speak against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, persecute {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and treat them violently. But I was shown mercy, because I did not know what I was doing in my unbelief,
and the grace of our Lord poured over me, along with the faith and love that are found in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

L.12: I give thanks to the one who has strengthened me, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus our Lord, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} considered me faithful, appointing [me] to service,
L.13: though I was formerly a blasphemer and a persecutor and a violent man. But I was shown mercy, because I acted ignorantly in unbelief,
L.14: and the grace of our Lord overflowed, with the faith and love that are in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.

R.12: I thank {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord, who makes me strong. I thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} trusted me and chose me to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.13: Before that, I said evil things against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I hurt {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and was cruel to them. But God showed me mercy, because I did not believe and did not know what I was doing.
R.14: Our Lord poured out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace on me, more than enough, and with it came the faith and love that we have in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

decisions.choice: I give thanks: I am grateful
decisions.reason: Χάριν is the word for grace, but in this phrase it means thanks (2 Timothy 1:3; Luke 17:9).

decisions.choice: a blasphemer, a persecutor, a violent man: Paul before his conversion
decisions.reason: Paul persecuted the church (Acts 8:3; 9:1-2; Galatians 1:13). To attack Christ's people was to speak against Christ (Acts 9:4-5). ὑβριστήν is someone who treats others with violent contempt.

decisions.choice: because I acted ignorantly in unbelief: why mercy was shown
decisions.reason: Paul does not excuse himself (verse 15 calls him the foremost of sinners); his ignorance put him among those for whom there is mercy (compare Luke 23:34; Numbers 15:27-31).

decisions.choice: overflowed: abounded beyond measure
decisions.reason: ὑπερεπλεόνασεν is a strengthened word, "abounded beyond all measure" (compare Romans 5:20).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: give thanks (L); thank (B, R)
decisions.reason: The sense here is thanks (m1), so the key term "grace" is not used for this word.

decisions.choice: speak against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, persecute {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people (B); said evil things against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, hurt {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people (R)
alternatives: a blasphemer and a persecutor and a violent man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who was blasphemed and persecuted (m2).

records.heading: Mercy for the worst of sinners

records.source: πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος, ὅτι Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἁμαρτωλοὺς σῶσαι· ὧν πρῶτός εἰμι ἐγώ, ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἠλεήθην, ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ πρώτῳ ἐνδείξηται Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς τὴν ἅπασαν μακροθυμίαν, πρὸς ὑποτύπωσιν τῶν μελλόντων πιστεύειν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
records.gloss: Trustworthy [is] the saying and of all acceptance worthy, that Christ Jesus came into the world sinners to save, of whom foremost am I; \v 16 but because of this I was shown mercy, so that in me foremost might display Christ Jesus the entire patience, as an example for those about to believe on him for life eternal.
pieces: Here is a saying you can rely on, which deserves to be fully accepted: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and I am the worst of them.

But I was shown mercy for this very reason: so that in me, the worst of all, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus could show how completely patient {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is, as an example for those who would come to believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and receive eternal life.

L.15: The saying [is] trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance, that {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am [the] foremost;
L.16: but for this reason I was shown mercy, so that in me, [the] foremost, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus might display {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} perfect patience as an example for those who were going to believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for eternal life.

R.15: Here is something true that everyone should believe: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus came into the world to save sinners. And I am the worst sinner of all.
R.16: But God showed me mercy. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} Jesus wanted to show how patient {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is, even with the worst sinner. So I am an example for people who will believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and receive eternal life.

decisions.choice: trustworthy is the saying: a formula introducing a known teaching
decisions.reason: This phrase is found only in the letters to Timothy and Titus (3:1; 4:9; 2 Timothy 2:11; Titus 3:8). It introduces a saying the churches knew and repeated.

decisions.choice: of whom I am the foremost: Paul still counts himself first among sinners
decisions.reason: The present εἰμι ("I am") is striking: Paul does not say "I was". πρῶτός can mean first in time or first in rank; with "worst" in view it is rank.

decisions.choice: an example: a pattern for others
decisions.reason: ὑποτύπωσιν is a pattern or model: if Christ was patient with Paul, no one is beyond his mercy.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the worst
decisions.reason: "Foremost" can sound like an honor; the sense is the worst (m2).

decisions.choice: Here is something true that everyone should believe
alternatives: The saying is trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance
decisions.reason: Readable puts the formula in plain words (m1).

records.source: τῷ δὲ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων, ἀφθάρτῳ, ἀοράτῳ, μόνῳ θεῷ, τιμὴ καὶ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
records.gloss: To the now King of the ages, immortal, invisible, only God, honor and glory to the ages of the ages; amen.
pieces: To the King of all ages, the immortal, invisible and only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

L.17: Now to the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, [be] honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

R.17: God is the King who rules forever. He will never die, and no one can see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is the only God. Let us give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

decisions.choice: the King of the ages: the eternal King
decisions.reason: τῶν αἰώνων is a Jewish title for God, the King who rules all the ages of time (Tobit 13:7, 13:11).

decisions.choice: immortal: not subject to decay or death
decisions.reason: ἀφθάρτῳ means incorruptible (Romans 1:23).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the only God"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "wise", probably from Romans 16:27.

decisions.choice: to the ages of the ages: forever and ever
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of saying for all eternity.

records.source: Ταύτην τὴν παραγγελίαν παρατίθεμαί σοι, τέκνον Τιμόθεε, κατὰ τὰς προαγούσας ἐπὶ σὲ προφητείας, ἵνα στρατεύῃ ἐν αὐταῖς τὴν καλὴν στρατείαν, ἔχων πίστιν καὶ ἀγαθὴν συνείδησιν, ἥν τινες ἀπωσάμενοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν ἐναυάγησαν·
records.gloss: This charge I entrust to you, child Timothy, according to the prophecies going before about you, so that you may fight by them the good fight, \v 19 holding faith and a good conscience, which some having rejected concerning the faith have suffered shipwreck;
pieces: Timothy, my son, I am entrusting you with this charge, in keeping with the prophecies once spoken over you, so that by following them you may fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a good conscience. Some have thrown their conscience aside, and their faith has been wrecked.

L.18: This charge I entrust to you, Timothy, [my] child, in keeping with the prophecies made earlier about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight,
L.19: holding faith and a good conscience. Some, rejecting [conscience], have suffered shipwreck in regard to the faith.

R.18: Timothy, my son, I am giving you this command. It agrees with the messages God gave about you in the past. Remember those messages, so that you can fight well for the Lord, like a good soldier.
R.19: Keep your faith, and do what you know is right. Some people have not listened to their conscience, and their faith has been destroyed, like a ship that sinks.

decisions.choice: the prophecies about you
decisions.reason: Prophetic words were spoken about Timothy, perhaps when he was set apart for his work (4:14; Acts 13:1-3).

decisions.choice: fight the good fight: serve as a soldier in a good campaign
decisions.reason: στρατεύομαι is to serve as a soldier; Paul uses military pictures for the work of the gospel (2 Timothy 2:3-4).

decisions.choice: rejecting conscience, they suffered shipwreck: their faith was wrecked
decisions.reason: ἥν refers to "good conscience". To push conscience away is to wreck one's faith, like a ship broken up on the rocks (ναυαγέω).

decisions.choice: my son
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: fight well for the Lord, like a good soldier; like a ship that sinks
alternatives: fight the good fight; suffered shipwreck
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two pictures (m2, m3).

records.heading: Timothy's charge

records.source: ὧν ἐστιν Ὑμέναιος καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος, οὓς παρέδωκα τῷ Σατανᾷ ἵνα παιδευθῶσι μὴ βλασφημεῖν.
records.gloss: of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to the Satan so that they may be taught not to blaspheme.
pieces: Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan so that they may learn not to blaspheme.

L.20: Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that they may be taught not to blaspheme.

R.20: Hymenaeus and Alexander are two of these people. I have put them out of the church and given them over to Satan, so that they will learn not to speak against God.

decisions.choice: Hymenaeus and Alexander
decisions.reason: A Hymenaeus is named again in 2 Timothy 2:17 as teaching that the resurrection had already happened; an Alexander appears in 2 Timothy 4:14. It is not certain they are the same men.

decisions.choice: handed over to Satan: put out of the church, for their correction
decisions.reason: As in 1 Corinthians 5:5, being handed over to Satan means being put outside the fellowship of the church, into the realm Satan rules. The purpose is correction: παιδεύω is to train or discipline, as a parent does.

decisions.choice: put them out of the church and given them over to Satan
decisions.reason: Readable says what being handed over to Satan means (m2).
